decisions.rationale: The deterministic Mkhedruli syllable mapping is directly supported by Georgian State Language Department transcription guidance, including the relevant CV sequences and YA /ja/ -> ია, with ISO 9984:2026 as an independent script-standard reference.

The deterministic mapping targets Eastern Armenian phonetic values and is supported by the Library of Congress Armenian romanization table plus ISO 9985:2026. Western Armenian is explicitly outside this profile.

A fully vocalized Arabic display profile preserves canonical A/I/U distinctions mechanically through fatḥa, kasra and ḍamma. Full vocalization is intentionally more explicit than ordinary adult prose and is part of the profile definition.

The Hindi-oriented Devanagari adaptation follows the Government of India principle of approximating standard pronunciation for international terms and explicitly documents vowel-quality/quantity approximation and nukta ज़ for /z/.

Government of Bangladesh dictionary evidence resolves both previous blockers: foreign initial y- is represented with ইয়া-/ইয়া-, while foreign z- is routinely adapted with জ (for example zebra → জেব্রা and zone → জোন). The profile therefore uses YA=ইয়া and ZU=জু, with the Bengali /z/→জ realization documented as a language-specific approximation rather than inventing জ়.

ALA-LC and Unicode resolve the vowel-system blocker: modern Persian distinguishes short /e,o/ from /i,u/, and the regular written values for the latter are ی/و. The reviewed mapping therefore uses MI/NI/etc. with ی and MU/NU/etc. with و, explicitly accepting vowel-length approximation instead of misusing Persian kasra/damma as canonical /i,u/.
